title: ML supervisado y baselines responsables
scope: LESSONS_ONLY: title/tagline/job relevance, learning outcomes, theory/reference paragraphs, theory code/output, callouts and figures. I Do / We Do / You Do / self-check / exams remain outside this campaign.

live_status.public_tagline: comparación honesta que conserva el baseline determinista y demuestra cuándo el ML agrega —o no agrega— valor

roadmap_contract.T1: unidad, target, horizonte, costos, baseline de regla y dummy
roadmap_contract.T2: regresión/logística y regularización; coeficientes, supuestos y scaling
roadmap_contract.T3: árboles/ensambles, Random Forest/boosting, overfit, profundidad y reproducibilidad
roadmap_contract.T4: pipeline, tracking, validación cruzada apropiada y error analysis
roadmap_contract.gate: comparación honesta que conserva el baseline determinista y demuestra cuándo el ML agrega —o no agrega— valor

prior_audit_comparison.reason: Current canonical source has substantial added neural-network, framework and temporal-validation material, and runtime counterexamples contradict the old report's strong-quality conclusion.

external_research.relevance: Start simple, choose observable objectives, measure baselines before complexity.
Never fit preprocessing on test; Pipeline helps avoid leakage.
Most-frequent baseline is fit on training y then used for predictions; it is not re-fit on validation labels.
Logistic regression is a fitted classifier; C is inverse regularization strength.
penalty argument is deprecated from 1.8; current future-facing material needs a version pin or updated l1_ratio formulation.
Non-overlapping groups must be enforced for every fold; one group id per sample is insufficient when one pair sample contains two independently reusable entity endpoints.
Time-ordered validation must not train on future observations.
PyTorch development began in 2016 and the project launched in 2017; source wording says it was published in 2016.
TensorFlow 2 enables eager execution by default and can compile graph functions; the source's TF1-vs-PyTorch historical caveat is broadly defensible.

observations: dummy_and_cost([0,1,2]) treats a multiclass label list as if it were the binary target contract
prevalence=sum(y)/len(y) is meaningless for non-binary labels

runtime_counterexamples.input: y=['a','b'] with equal counts, max(set(y), key=y.count)

observations: pred_at(..., x=NaN) returns 0 because NaN >= threshold is False

runtime_counterexamples.output: ranked=['amount_z','shared_phone'], sign='neg'; a caller printing this as sign_shared_phone would mislabel the sign

runtime_counterexamples.note: No params, feature_set, split, data/model identity or cost are required.

runtime_counterexamples.output: beats_dummy=True while candidate is strictly worse than the documented rule baseline

runtime_counterexamples.observation: The shared RNG is advanced by entrena(True) before entrena(False); the two variants start from different W1/W2 matrices.

findings.evidence: S33 states it reuses S32 features already clean of leakage, while S32 is REPAIR_REQUIRED with 37 findings.
findings.attack: A downstream model can legitimize broken relational and temporal features merely by fitting on them.
findings.defense: S33 could use its own synthetic independent fixture.
findings.impact: The S32→S33 contract is not machine-valid and the prerequisite gate is bypassed.
findings.proposed_change: Require an actually promoted S32 feature-set manifest before any S33 fit/evaluation.

findings.evidence: Theory references shared_phone and amount_z as clean, but no catalog/schema hash, fitted-state hash, feature_set manifest or as-of provenance is consumed.
findings.attack: A column name is treated as evidence of feature correctness.
findings.defense: The source verbally references fs-vN from S32.
findings.impact: Train runs cannot prove which S32 transformation produced their features.
findings.proposed_change: Bind every run to feature_set_id + catalog hash + fitted-state hash + source snapshot/cutoff.

findings.evidence: Core theory blocks end in print outputs or hard-coded flags; there is no pytest gate despite systematic pytest being required since S27.
findings.attack: Broken comparisons can return exit code 0.
findings.defense: The snippets are didactic demonstrations.
findings.impact: The section called 'responsible baselines' does not mechanically reject irresponsible runs.
findings.proposed_change: Turn framing, baseline, pipeline, split, CV and promotion invariants into real pytest tests.

findings.evidence: needs_review_7d is defined as whether a case 'debería entrar' into review, while the outcome calls it observable.
findings.attack: 'Should review' is a normative policy judgment, not an observed event unless an explicit labeling protocol defines it.
findings.defense: It intentionally avoids a fraud label.
findings.impact: The learner can train on an ambiguous policy label and mistake it for ground truth.
findings.proposed_change: Define the exact observable event/labeler/policy version and distinguish observed queue entry from adjudicated review need.

findings.evidence: frame_task only checks substring 'fraud'. It does not enforce needs_review_*, horizon>0, or agreement between target suffix and horizon.
findings.attack: Invalid framing passes the canonical helper.
findings.defense: The callout states the intended restrictions.
findings.impact: Prose fail-closed policy is not implemented.
findings.proposed_change: Parse and validate an allowlisted TaskSpec with unit, target family, horizon and target/horizon consistency.

findings.evidence: A 7-day future target is introduced without requiring the full 7-day outcome window to have elapsed for each training label.
findings.attack: Recent examples can be falsely labeled negative merely because their horizon has not matured.
findings.defense: All examples are synthetic and tiny.
findings.impact: Right-censoring can contaminate training/evaluation labels.
findings.proposed_change: Require label_cutoff >= origin+horizon and record label maturity/censoring status.

findings.evidence: prevalence=sum(y)/len(y) and dummy_and_cost assume non-empty binary numeric labels without checking them.
findings.attack: Empty or multiclass/invalid labels crash or produce meaningless prevalence/cost.
findings.defense: Fixtures use 0/1.
findings.impact: The executable contract is narrower than the prose without fail-closed validation.
findings.proposed_change: Validate support>0 and label domain exactly {0,1}; report positive support and prevalence.

findings.evidence: S33-overfit-gap is attached to T1-A unit/target/horizon and its alt says train/test/baseline although overfit is taught later using train-valid.
findings.attack: A future concept and inconsistent split name are injected before their explanation.
findings.defense: It previews the section's later problem.
findings.impact: Unnecessary cognitive load and test/validation terminology drift.
findings.proposed_change: Move the figure to T3-B and use train/valid consistently.

findings.evidence: dummy_and_cost(y) derives majority from the same y on which accuracy/cost are measured.
findings.attack: On a holdout whose prevalence changes, the baseline sees validation labels before predicting them; runtime counterexample turns a proper 0% into 100%.
findings.defense: The tiny fixture is not explicitly labeled train or valid.
findings.impact: The baseline itself is leaked, invalidating the central comparison.
findings.proposed_change: Fit majority on y_train, freeze it, then evaluate predictions on y_valid/test.

findings.evidence: Comment says max(set(y), key=y.count) chooses the smaller class on ties. Python max returns the first maximal element encountered, while set is unordered.
findings.attack: Equal-count general labels change with hash seed; runtime reproduced both 'a' and 'b'.
findings.defense: The canonical binary int fixture commonly yields 0.
findings.impact: A documented deterministic policy is not actually guaranteed by the implementation.
findings.proposed_change: Count labels and explicitly select min(label) among tied maxima.

findings.evidence: Rule x>=thr is evaluated, but no training-only selection/freeze provenance exists for thr.
findings.attack: Choosing thr after inspecting validation/test makes the simple baseline itself tuned to the answer.
findings.defense: thr=1.0 can be interpreted as a predeclared domain rule.
findings.impact: The code cannot distinguish a prior heuristic from a post-hoc optimized rule.
findings.proposed_change: Record rule_id/version, threshold source and train-only selection or pre-model domain provenance before holdout evaluation.

findings.evidence: Canonical code computes FP/FN cost only for the dummy; rule and candidate costs are absent.
findings.attack: A model can improve accuracy while making the expensive error type worse.
findings.defense: The prose repeatedly says cost matters.
findings.impact: The declared business objective is not comparable across alternatives.
findings.proposed_change: Evaluate identical cost function on dummy, rule and candidate predictions on the same examples.

findings.evidence: beats_dummy is acc > dummy_acc even though opening warns accuracy is misleading under imbalance and costs are asymmetric.
findings.attack: Runtime shows candidate accuracy .70 beats dummy .667 while rule is 1.0; worse-cost candidates can also pass.
findings.defense: Text says winning dummy alone is not enough when rule is stronger.
findings.impact: The executable flag contradicts the lesson's own responsible-baseline doctrine.
findings.proposed_change: Define promotion against the best frozen baseline on predeclared primary metric/cost, with secondary metrics recorded separately.

findings.evidence: Dummy/rule, logistic, stump and tracking examples use disconnected handcrafted inputs/metrics rather than one held-out dataset/split.
findings.attack: No number demonstrates incremental value because candidates are not evaluated on the same examples under the same metric contract.
findings.defense: Each subtopic isolates one concept pedagogically.
findings.impact: The section's headline gate is never actually executed end to end.
findings.proposed_change: Create one frozen synthetic train/valid/test fixture and evaluate every baseline/candidate on the same valid/test rows.

findings.evidence: logistic.py hard-codes w=1,b=0 and a params dict; it never optimizes logistic loss or fits a regularized classifier.
findings.attack: The section promises supervised ML and regularization but demonstrates only the sigmoid function.
findings.defense: The goal may be to understand mechanics before APIs.
findings.impact: The required T2 competence—fit a regularized logistic baseline—is not demonstrated.
findings.proposed_change: Fit a real train-only logistic model (or implement a tiny optimizer) and evaluate frozen predictions against baselines.

findings.evidence: Future-facing text teaches sklearn penalty='l2' + C. Current scikit-learn 1.8+ deprecates penalty and current docs express penalty choice via l1_ratio, while C remains inverse strength.
findings.attack: A learner following current API guidance receives stale parameter advice unless the course pins an older sklearn contract.
findings.defense: The snippet does not import sklearn and the L2 concept remains correct.
findings.impact: Concept-to-library bridge is time-sensitive and presently underspecified.
findings.proposed_change: Pin the sklearn version for the lesson or teach the current l1_ratio/C API with a version note.

findings.evidence: sigmoid(-1000) overflows and pred_at with NaN silently returns 0.
findings.attack: Non-finite/big-magnitude inputs turn numerical invalidity into a negative class or exception.
findings.defense: Toy inputs are small and finite.
findings.impact: An advanced model gate should distinguish invalid score from valid non-priority prediction.
findings.proposed_change: Validate finite z/x and use a numerically stable expit implementation.

findings.evidence: scaled=True and causal=False are hard-coded prints; rank_coefs does not receive scale metadata. It also returns the sign of the top feature, then the example labels it sign_shared_phone.
findings.attack: Changing coefficients can make amount_z top while the printed variable still claims the sign belongs to shared_phone.
findings.defense: Current fixture keeps shared_phone top.
findings.impact: The interpretability guardrails are presentation flags rather than validated model metadata.
findings.proposed_change: Bind coefficient rows to feature names, scale state and fold/model version; report sign per feature.

findings.evidence: A five-paragraph neural-network/XOR block is added although the authoritative S33 roadmap does not require neural networks and explicitly requires RF/boosting/pipeline/CV competencies that remain unimplemented.
findings.attack: High cognitive-cost optional material displaces required gate work.
findings.defense: The block is labeled optional for later sections.
findings.impact: Progressive disclosure is weakened exactly where core supervised-evaluation skills are incomplete.
findings.proposed_change: Move the NN block to an optional appendix/appropriate later section until required S33 gates are executable.

findings.evidence: red_diminuta.py shares one RNG; entrena(True) consumes random weights before entrena(False), so activation/no-activation variants start from different parameters.
findings.attack: The text calls it the same network without activation, but two factors change at once.
findings.defense: Without a nonlinearity the architecture cannot solve XOR regardless of initialization.
findings.impact: The ablation is methodologically uncontrolled and exact loss comparison is not attributable solely to tanh.
findings.proposed_change: Clone identical initial weights for both variants or reset independent RNGs to the same seed before each fit.

findings.evidence: Text says a small neural network 'casi nunca gana' a well-made logistic regression on tabular data.
findings.attack: Nonlinear tabular problems can strongly favor nonlinear models; the claim lacks scope/evidence.
findings.defense: It is intended to discourage unjustified complexity.
findings.impact: A good complexity-control lesson becomes a false empirical rule.
findings.proposed_change: Say the network must beat a strong logistic baseline on this dataset; do not predict the winner generically.

findings.evidence: T4-A says Meta's lab 'publicó PyTorch' in 2016. PyTorch Foundation history says development began in 2016 and PyTorch launched in 2017.
findings.attack: Historical date is wrong.
findings.defense: 2016 is genuinely the development-start year.
findings.impact: Avoidable factual error in a nonessential tangent.
findings.proposed_change: Use 'el desarrollo comenzó en 2016 y el lanzamiento público llegó en 2017'.

findings.evidence: T4-A asserts 2026 PyTorch dominance in research/production and names Meta/OpenAI/Tesla without a learner-visible current source.
findings.attack: Labor/usage share is time-sensitive and source-dependent; official PyTorch material supports broad research/production adoption, not this precise comparative labor-market claim.
findings.defense: PyTorch is undeniably a primary research/production platform and TensorFlow remains widely used.
findings.impact: A transient market assertion distracts from S33 and can age rapidly.
findings.proposed_change: Remove the ranking claim or cite a dated methodology and label it as a snapshot, not a durable curriculum fact.

findings.evidence: stump.py applies a hand-provided threshold and a hand-provided list of votes; no split criterion or stump is learned from labeled training data.
findings.attack: A supervised tree lesson is reduced to thresholding and voting mechanics.
findings.defense: The source explicitly calls it a controlled stump illustration.
findings.impact: The learner never demonstrates that a tree candidate learned from data or beat the baselines.
findings.proposed_change: Fit/select a stump using train-only labels and score it on the frozen validation data.

findings.evidence: majority_vote([]) returns 1; depth_unlimited=False is printed as a literal rather than derived from a model/configuration.
findings.attack: Empty ensemble and model-depth policy both false-green.
findings.defense: Fixtures provide three votes and no real tree object.
findings.impact: The 'controlled ensemble' safeguards are not safeguards.
findings.proposed_change: Reject empty votes and read/validate max_depth from the fitted candidate configuration.

findings.evidence: Authoritative roadmap names Random Forest/boosting; theory explicitly says it will not practice either and only shows stump+vote.
findings.attack: A required topic is deliberately omitted while unrelated neural-network/framework material is added.
findings.defense: Stumps can introduce ensemble intuition with lower cognitive load.
findings.impact: The section does not satisfy its authoritative T3 contract.
findings.proposed_change: Add minimal fitted RF/boosting comparisons or formally revise the roadmap; do not silently substitute a different competency.

findings.evidence: seeded_ints calls global random.seed; prose equates a seed with auditable reproducibility.
findings.attack: Global reseeding changes unrelated consumers, and reproducibility also depends on data/split/code/library/model versions.
findings.defense: The snippet only demonstrates seeded pseudo-random numbers.
findings.impact: Seed is taught as a stronger guarantee than it is.
findings.proposed_change: Use a local RNG and log seed together with data, split, feature-set, code and library versions.

findings.evidence: Prose says best depth is selected by validation/cost, but code only evaluates an already supplied train_acc/valid_acc gap.
findings.attack: No candidate depths are fit, compared or frozen.
findings.defense: The outcome emphasizes detecting overfit rather than hyperparameter search.
findings.impact: The claimed control of depth is not demonstrated.
findings.proposed_change: Evaluate a small predeclared depth grid on train/valid (inside correct CV) and freeze the selected depth before test.

findings.evidence: T4-A is titled 'Pipeline y tracking mínimo', but tracking.py has no preprocessing/model Pipeline and no S32 feature-set binding.
findings.attack: The required S33 pipeline construct is absent.
findings.defense: S32 introduced a conceptual pipeline.
findings.impact: Preprocessing can be fit outside folds and model runs cannot be reproduced end to end.
findings.proposed_change: Use a real Pipeline/ColumnTransformer + estimator bound to the S32 manifest and split contract.

findings.evidence: run_fields lists params but log_valid never receives/checks them; beats_rule/cost are absent; feature_set/data/split/model versions and finite metrics are unvalidated.
findings.attack: Runtime accepts {'accuracy':0.5}, run_id='run', beats=False as a valid logged run without params.
findings.defense: This is labeled 'tracking mínimo'.
findings.impact: The minimum log is too weak to reproduce or compare the experiment it claims to document.
findings.proposed_change: Require immutable run manifest with params, feature_set, data/split refs, seed, model/code version, baseline metrics/cost and all evaluation metrics.

findings.evidence: tracking example introduces f1 as a metric, while the roadmap teaches F-score in S34 and S33 never defines F1.
findings.attack: A next-section metric appears as if already learned.
findings.defense: F1 is common ML vocabulary and not manipulated here.
findings.impact: Widow term breaks progressive disclosure for the ZERO_TECH learner model.
findings.proposed_change: Either define F1 briefly or keep S33 tracking to metrics already taught and introduce F1 in S34.

findings.evidence: Four long PyTorch/TensorFlow/history/job-market paragraphs are embedded inside 'Pipeline y tracking mínimo', while the code remains tracking.py and contains no frameworks.
findings.attack: The section interrupts the causal sequence experiment→pipeline→CV with an unrelated framework survey.
findings.defense: It gives career context after the optional NN block.
findings.impact: High extraneous cognitive load and weak connective tissue around the most important experiment-governance block.
findings.proposed_change: Move the framework survey to an optional later resource/appendix; keep T4-A focused on reproducible experiment pipelines.

findings.evidence: group_cv.py receives precomputed fold scores and prints one disjoint train/valid pair; it never constructs folds, fits a model or evaluates predictions per fold.
findings.attack: The section claims group CV without executing cross-validation.
findings.defense: The helper demonstrates the disjointness invariant.
findings.impact: Core T4 validation competency is missing.
findings.proposed_change: Use actual grouped split indices and fit the full pipeline separately inside every training fold.

findings.evidence: Only train_fold0/valid_fold0 are checked; random_leak_ok=False is a hard-coded print.
findings.attack: Another fold can contain overlap while the canonical output remains green.
findings.defense: The fixture has only one illustrated fold.
findings.impact: A partial check is presented as group-CV evidence.
findings.proposed_change: Validate every fold and derive the random/group policy result from the actual splitter.

findings.evidence: The declared scoring unit is entity_pair, but group CV models each sample with one entity id. A pair has two reusable endpoints.
findings.attack: Train pair (e1,e2) and valid pair (e2,e3) can share e2 even if a single chosen group label differs, leaking identity across folds.
findings.defense: Some datasets may define one canonical case owner/group per sample.
findings.impact: The proposed grouping representation cannot guarantee the invariant the prose claims for pair samples.
findings.proposed_change: For pairwise data, construct folds so neither endpoint appears across train/valid—e.g. assign connected components of entity-overlap or another explicit multi-entity grouping policy.

findings.evidence: No S32 imputer/scaler/vocabulary Pipeline is fit inside each training fold.
findings.attack: Even with disjoint IDs, preprocessing fit globally before CV would leak validation information.
findings.defense: S32 already explained train-only fit.
findings.impact: The transition S32→S33 fails to apply the very leakage rule S32 exists to teach.
findings.proposed_change: Wrap preprocessing+estimator in one pipeline and fit it independently in each fold.

findings.evidence: mean_fold([]) divides by zero; fold support/validity is not stored with the mean.
findings.attack: Missing folds can crash or a mean can be reported without sample/group support.
findings.defense: Canonical fixture always has three folds.
findings.impact: The experiment summary lacks basic denominator evidence.
findings.proposed_change: Reject empty folds and log per-fold support/groups/metric before aggregate mean/std.

findings.evidence: T4-B says error analysis inspects the slice with most FN, but no code constructs pair-level errors or any slice table.
findings.attack: A required roadmap competency is pure narration.
findings.defense: S34 deepens metrics and imbalance later.
findings.impact: S33 cannot explain where its candidate fails before handoff to S34.
findings.proposed_change: Persist pair_id, gold, pred, score and slice attributes; compute at least one FN/FP slice with support.

findings.evidence: The final T4-B block switches from binary needs_review_7d classification to univariate daily review-load forecasting evaluated by MAE.
findings.attack: Unit, target, estimator family and metric all change inside the same gate without an explicit new task contract.
findings.defense: The intent is to teach time-aware validation generally.
findings.impact: Learner cannot connect the temporal-validation evidence back to the workbench classifier being promoted.
findings.proposed_change: Demonstrate rolling-origin/temporal splitting on the same classification task or label this as a separate optional forecasting example.

findings.evidence: At origin 7 with horizon 7, the 'ayer' predictor for validation indices 8..13 reads serie[7..12], which are actual values inside the validation horizon.
findings.attack: It is a rolling one-step baseline compared against a fixed-origin 7-day seasonal baseline while text says all 7 next days are predicted from the origin.
findings.defense: If production observes each previous day before predicting the next, yesterday is a legitimate rolling baseline.
findings.impact: The two baselines do not share the same information set, invalidating the reported 1.10 vs 3.86 comparison for the stated fixed-origin task.
findings.proposed_change: Either recursively predict the full horizon using only origin-available data or explicitly change the evaluation to daily rolling one-step updates for every candidate.

findings.evidence: frontera_respetada checks integer index order only; the source acknowledges some systems need both group and time constraints but implements no combined policy or feature/label availability gap.
findings.attack: Temporal ordering alone can still leak the same entity or not-yet-mature labels/features.
findings.defense: The block isolates the time dependency concept.
findings.impact: 'appropriate CV' remains unresolved for the actual pairwise, horizon-based workbench.
findings.proposed_change: Implement a domain splitter that enforces time origin/horizon plus pair/entity non-overlap and label/feature availability where required.

findings.evidence: origen_movil.py compares two naive baselines only; no S33 candidate model is evaluated on those folds.
findings.attack: The block cannot demonstrate whether ML adds value under temporal validation.
findings.defense: Its purpose is baseline discipline.
findings.impact: The closing temporal lesson remains disconnected from the headline S33 gate.
findings.proposed_change: Evaluate the frozen candidate and all baselines on exactly the same temporal folds/information set.

findings.evidence: No canonical function blocks promotion based on best baseline, cost, split validity, S32 manifest, or CV results. Job relevance mentions dummy; theory later admits rule may be stronger.
findings.attack: A model can be labeled beats_dummy=True and still lose to the rule, cost objective or invalid split.
findings.defense: The prose repeatedly states such a model should not be promoted.
findings.impact: The section's headline gate is advisory text rather than an executable decision.
findings.proposed_change: Create a promotion function that requires valid upstream manifest/splits and candidate improvement over the best frozen baseline on the predeclared primary objective.

findings.evidence: S33-baseline-gap visual compares majority/logistic/complex model but omits the simple rule that the section calls the second mandatory baseline.
findings.attack: The visual model makes 'baseline' look singular when the lesson later requires dual anchors.
findings.defense: A figure can simplify the comparison.
findings.impact: It weakens the core idea that ML must beat the strongest simple alternative, not merely majority.
findings.proposed_change: Include both dummy and rule baselines or label the chart explicitly as one illustrative baseline only.

findings.evidence: The reference block says T4 closes with experiment logging + group CV and lists the roadmap sequence, but current theory also contains a five-paragraph NN block, a four-paragraph framework survey and a second temporal T4-B block.
findings.attack: The learner-facing map no longer describes the actual section they must navigate.
findings.defense: Some additions are optional/extension material.
findings.impact: Connective tissue is stale after source expansion from the older 28-paragraph version to the current 46-paragraph theory.
findings.proposed_change: Either move extensions out or update the map with explicit optional/extension branches without pretending they are part of the core gate.

rejected_findings.suspicion: Using simple baselines before complex ML is simplistic.
rejected_findings.reason: Google's Rules of ML and current experiment guidance explicitly support simple baselines and tracking losing experiments.

rejected_findings.suspicion: C being inverse regularization strength is wrong.
rejected_findings.reason: Current scikit-learn documentation confirms smaller C means stronger regularization.

rejected_findings.suspicion: Group-aware validation is unnecessary if time split exists.
rejected_findings.reason: Group and time dependencies answer different generalization problems; current sklearn guidance explicitly treats grouped and time-series CV separately.

rejected_findings.suspicion: TensorFlow today is purely static-graph while PyTorch is purely eager/dynamic.
rejected_findings.reason: The source correctly qualifies the static-graph contrast as TensorFlow 1.x and notes TensorFlow 2 eager execution; current TensorFlow docs confirm eager is default while tf.function can create graphs.
The source explicitly says association in the model is not causality/fraud proof.

rejected_findings.suspicion: A run that loses the baseline should be discarded.
rejected_findings.reason: The source correctly teaches that a losing but reproducible run remains valuable experiment evidence; Google experiment guidance agrees.

highest_risk_findings: S33-F09 dummy baseline is fit on the evaluation labels and can turn a proper 0% holdout baseline into 100%
S33-F04/F05/F06 target is not operationally observable/validated/mature despite being called observable
S33-F12/F13/F14 candidate comparison ignores consistent cost/best-baseline/same-holdout evaluation
S33-F15 logistic regression is never fit; L2 is a params label rather than training evidence
S33-F29/F33/F36 required Pipeline/CV does not fit preprocessing+model within folds
S33-F35 pairwise unit can leak an entity across folds because one group id cannot represent two endpoints
S33-F40 yesterday temporal baseline consumes validation-horizon actuals and is incomparable to the fixed-origin seasonal baseline
S33-F43 no executable promotion gate exists

USABLE: Simple baseline-first thinking is valid and strongly supported externally.
A losing experiment should still be logged.
C is inverse regularization strength in sklearn logistic regression.
Scaled coefficient sign is an association within the model, not causal proof.
Group and temporal dependencies require different validation designs.
Rolling/expanding temporal validation is conceptually useful when the information set is kept honest.
MISCONCEPTION_RISK: majority computed from evaluation y = valid dummy baseline
max(set(y), key=y.count) = guaranteed smallest tie class
penalty label in params = evidence a regularized fit occurred
accuracy beats dummy = candidate deserves promotion
same single entity group id is enough for entity_pair leakage control
precomputed fold scores + one disjoint check = group CV
yesterday baseline inside a seven-day fixed-origin holdout uses only origin-known information
fs-vN/column names alone = clean S32 feature provenance
